chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not eat from the slaughtered meat of the Magian of the Magian.' He said, and he said: 'Do not eat from the slaughtered meat of the Christians of Taghlib, for they are the polytheists of the Arabs.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat slaughtered by Magians and Christians of Taghlib according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic distinction between the People of the Book and other monotheistic sects, specifically classifying the Taghlib Christians as *mushrikū al-'Arab* due to their unique theological syncretism. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the actual religious status of a group rather than their nominal title, influencing the fiqh of *dhabihah* regarding non-Muslim slaughterers.
